contribution: Architected the client-side parsing pipeline, deterministic scoring algorithms, semantic skill extraction, optional Gemini/Claude structured bullet rewrites (X-Y-Z formula), and 35 automated Vitest unit and integration tests.
features: Local-first client parsing via Mozilla PDF.js guaranteeing zero resume data transmission to external servers.
7-dimension weighted scoring engine evaluating typography, formatting, contact hygiene, ATS parseability, bullet strength, and structural completeness.
6-layer semantic skill matching engine comparing candidate profiles against target job descriptions.
Optional Google Gemini 2.5 Flash / Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet structured bullet optimizer implementing Google's X-Y-Z accomplishment formula.

title: Credit Card Approval Prediction (CreditGuard AI)
summary: An end-to-end Machine Learning pipeline evaluating applicant credit delinquency risk using a Calibrated Random Forest model with cost-sensitive cutoffs and local SHAP explainability.
problem: Financial institutions face severe credit default losses from asymmetric misclassification costs, where false negatives (unflagged defaulters) are far costlier than false positives.
solution: Trained and benchmarked multiple classifiers (Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost, Logistic Regression); selected Calibrated Random Forest as the production champion achieving 97.97% accuracy, 0.7865 ROC-AUC, 0.015387 Brier score (-14.0% error improvement vs uncalibrated), and a cost-sensitive decision cutoff (p* = 0.0395 at 5:1 penalty) delivering 35.77% delinquency recall with local SHAP interpretability.
contribution: Engineered feature pipelines on 438k records, implemented sigmoid probability calibration, optimized 5:1 cost-sensitive decision cutoffs, built Flask 3.0 inference service with Dark/Light dashboard, and integrated de-duplicated local SHAP explanations.
features: Production champion Calibrated Random Forest delivering 97.97% accuracy, 0.7865 ROC-AUC, and 0.015387 Brier score (-14.0% probability error reduction).
Asymmetric 5:1 cost-sensitive decision threshold optimization at p* = 0.0395, capturing 35.77% default recall on imbalanced credit data.
Local TreeSHAP explainability engine providing transparent feature contribution waterfalls for individual credit decisions.
Production Flask 3.0 web application with responsive UI, Dark/Light modes, SQLite storage, Docker containerization, and GitHub Actions CI/CD.
verifiedResult: 97.97% Accuracy • 0.7865 ROC-AUC • 0.015387 Brier Score (-14% Error) • 35.77% Default Recall

title: Amazon ML Challenge 2026 — Entity Resolution
summary: A high-throughput, memory-bounded machine learning pipeline resolving merchant identity across millions of noisy commercial records without pretrained embedding models.
problem: Matching identical business entities across heterogeneous data sources with noisy names, partial addresses, and severe class imbalance at scale (1.7M+ test anchors).
solution: Built a scalable candidate generation inverted index and 19-feature LightGBM classification pipeline with hard-negative mining, calibrated thresholding, and streaming validation.
contribution: Developed custom inverted index with token-frequency weighting, 19 rapid pairwise similarity features (RapidFuzz Normalized Indel, token overlap, numeric conflicts), and zero-leakage partition streaming.
features: Engineered multi-token inverted index processing 207M+ candidate links across 1.73M anchors with 0.9118 holdout candidate recall.
Extracted 19 pairwise similarity and interaction features with memory-mapped Arrow stores and deterministic tie-breaking.
Trained hard-negative LightGBM achieving 0.8879 Macro F0.5 (0.9563 Precision, 0.8053 Recall) on local 5,000-anchor calibration holdout.
Validated end-to-end pipeline with 39 automated tests and streaming compliance checks.
verifiedResult: 0.8879 Local Holdout Macro F0.5 (0.9563 Precision) across 39 verified unit and streaming tests
